jobs.description: Location : Fully Remote (Global) Classification : Full-time; 40 hours per week Pay Range : €51,000-90,000 Experience : 2+ years as a QA engineer Welcome to Miaplaza! Our vision is to elevate online learning by applying the most successful approaches in virtual education to create an accessible and inclusive homeschool curriculum platform where all students can be successful! Our K-8 platforms include Miacademy , Always Icecream , and Clever Dragons , and our 9-12 options include MiaPrep and MiaPrep Online High School . Our student base is rapidly growing, and we’re hiring for multiple positions across several departments! Our expansion stems from our commitment to providing exceptional educational content and our pursuit of new opportunities. 🚀 ▶️ You can hear our CEO, Johannes Ziegler, discuss our company’s values and future ! How you’ll make an impact (position summary): Miaplaza is dedicated to making education engaging and accessible through innovative online learning platforms. The Role We're looking for a QA Engineer to join our current QA team. You'll take ownership of how we test, validate, and sign off on quality across our platform. We're actively investing in our QA practice: expanding automated test coverage, improving our release testing process, and moving toward a model where quality is embedded throughout the development lifecycle. You'll report to a technical Engineering Manager and work alongside engineers who value clear test documentation, reliable automation, and confident code releases. As a mature company, we have legacy systems and established manual testing workflows, but we are transitioning to modern automated testing practices using Playwright and TypeScript. The split between manual and automated work varies, but you should be comfortable working across both, bringing automation where it adds the most value while pragmatically maintaining manual coverage where it's still the right tool. A core goal of our QA evolution is to make testing faster, more reliable, and less dependent on last-minute changes before each release: replacing fragile manual regression cycles with stable automated suites, reducing flakiness, and building coverage that the whole team can rely on. Every testing investment is measured by whether it improves quality and reduces the team's burden at release time. What You'll Do Write and maintain automated regression tests; review automation MRs from peers Execute manual testing across web UIs (functional, regression, cross-platform, responsive layouts on mobile/tablet) Create and maintain test cases, checklists, and test documentation in TestRail File clear, actionable bug reports with reproduction steps; collaborate with developers to triage and resolve Own the release testing process to ensure only high-quality changes ship Partner with PMs and designers on requirements review, edge cases, and acceptance criteria Contribute to QA process improvements as we scale (currently a 2-person team growing to 4) How We Work We believe you should know what your days look like before you accept an offer. Here's the reality: Meetings (yes, we keep them minimal): Daily standup with your product team. Show up, share updates and unblock each other.. Sprint planning and retrospectives with your product team, once per sprint. 1:1 with your Engineering Manager - Regular cadence, your agenda. Monthly Engineering all-hands. That's it. The rest of your time is yours to work. Deployments: Bi-monthly release cadence with a schedule published in advance. As a QA Engineer, you own the release testing window. Coordinating with developers, running regression suites, and signing off on quality before the release. Infrequent ad-hoc hotfixes Communication: Async-friendly. Documentation-first. Slack/ Jira/ GitLab MRs/ Notion Google Workspace for email and documents. Zoom for video calls. Timezone: We need significant overlap with typical CET (Central European Time) working hours to coordinate and collaborate synchronously. Additionally we have stakeholders and developers in US timezones that we occasionally need to meet. jobs.title: Senior Test Automation Engineer (TeamCity)
jobs.description: If you want to build and own the automated testing platform that powers a core piece of developer infrastructure, this is for you. You will focus on writing high-impact code, removing engineering friction, and setting the technical direction for quality on TeamCity. About JetBrains We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale. What you’ll do As our user base grows and enterprise pipelines become more complex, ensuring the highest quality for TeamCity is critical for the people who depend on us daily. We are looking for a senior engineer to own the quality engineering platform behind TeamCity. This is not a manual testing role or a suite maintenance job. You will spend your time writing code, building the tooling and frameworks that enable dozens of product engineers to ship confidently, removing manual work surrounding releases, and making our developer experience measurably better. You will lead the technical direction for quality on a large, feature-rich product, bring practical AI approaches into the workflow where they genuinely add value, and collaborate across teams to help product engineers own their tests. Day to day, you will: Evolve the automated testing platform, including frameworks, infrastructure, reporting, and CI/CD chains. Identify slow, manual, or fragile parts of our engineering process – such as release automation, feedback loops, and test flakiness – and fix them at the root. Integrate AI into the quality workflow for test generation with guardrails, automated failure triage, and self-healing tests. Work directly with product teams to help them write and own their tests, review their contributions, and evangelize solid test design. Investigate failures and flakiness across both tests and product code to drive them to resolution. Participate in all stages of product development, from initial design through release, interacting with internal and external users. What you’ll bring An engineer’s approach to quality, preferring to build tools and automate processes rather than maintain legacy tasks. Strong architectural judgment and a commitment to writing clean, maintainable code. Practical curiosity about AI, with a clear point of view on where it genuinely helps and where it falls short. A habit of working independently without formal specifications, figuring out the product, and determining what matters most. Clear, direct communication skills and the initiative to walk up to developers and persuade teams to improve how they work. An interest in mentoring colleagues, setting technical standards, and sharing knowledge across teams. What you’ll need Advanced skills in Kotlin or Java, with a solid grasp of object-oriented design and design patterns. Hands-on experience building and maintaining test automation for complex, mission-critical backends, web services, or desktop applications. Proficiency with testing frameworks (TestNG or JUnit) and browser automation (Selenium WebDriver, Selenide, or Playwright). Experience with build automation tools such as Gradle or Maven, containerization using Docker or Podman, and reporting tools like Allure. Command of Git and a solid understanding of software testing principles and concurrent programming concepts. A proven track record of creating internal platform tools or developer-experience improvements that measurably speed up engineering workflows. Fluency in spoken and written English. What success looks like Success in this role means transforming our quality infrastructure into a seamless, fast, and reliable platform that engineering teams love to use. You will have eliminated major sources of manual release work, reduced test flakiness, and established automated feedback loops that let developers ship code with total confidence. Product engineers will independently write high-quality tests using your frameworks, and your pragmatic integration of AI tools will have measurably improved failure triage and test creation. Why join JetBrains? Strong base salary. We offer competitive pay that reflects your skills and experience. Flexible work location. Enjoy the freedom to work from home or from the office. Remote work. Spend up to 30 days per year working remotely from abroad. Extra time off. More days to relax, recharge, and do the things you love.</

Reframe your resume bullet points around architectural impact, framework ROI, and team enablement rather than routine test execution.
Add metrics to your resume highlighting test execution speedups, CI/CD build stability, or defect leakage reduction.

Focus less on hands-on script writing in interviews and more on how you design scalable automation frameworks, optimize CI/CD feedback loops, mentor team members, and drive quality engineering practices across the entire SDLC.
